column1: Sonar is driving the future of agent-centric software development. As the leader in AI code review and verification, we solve a critical problem: ensuring that software generated by AI-assisted developers or autonomous agents is reliable, secure, and maintainable.

Integrating seamlessly with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Gemini, and Devin, we help over 75% of the Fortune 100 build trusted, reliable, compliant software. Customers who use Sonar are 44% less likely to report an outage due to AI-generated code.

We believe code verification is the critical missing link in the Agent-Centric Development Cycle (AC/DC). Industry giants like Nvidia, ServiceNow, Booking.com, Goldman Sachs, AstraZeneca, and Ford Motor Company count on us to provide independent, explainable, consistent review and governance of their AI-generated code via products like:
SonarQube: The world's leading AI code review and verification platform.
SonarQube Foundation Agent: Currently topping the leaderboards for agentic software repair.

column2: Sonar Context Augmentation: Providing the enterprise-grade context and constraints agents need to be truly effective.

column1: Our team operates across global hubs in Austin, Bochum, Dubai, Geneva, London, Singapore, Tokyo, and Washington D.C. We move with a mindset we call CODE:
Committed to our customers and community.

With over $400M in revenue and profitable, fast-paced growth, we are building the backbone of the AI software revolution. If you're hungry to have an impact, want to build at a fast pace, and ready to work at the forefront of AI, we want to hear from you.

As an Agentic Software Engineer on the Platform Architecture squad, you will build the multi-agent systems that autonomously refactor and modernize Sonar's own codebase — starting with one of our biggest technical bets: unifying SonarQube Cloud (SQC) and SonarQube Server (SQS) onto a single, portable architecture (""build once, deploy twice""). You will:

Design and build agentic refactoring pipelines that can safely extract a domain's logic from our existing SQS/SQC codebases and re-platform it onto our Unified Core (a hexagonal ""capability-core + adapters"" architecture), with minimal human oversight.

Define the guardrails that make autonomous refactoring safe at scale — verification gates, automated test generation, static analysis, and rollback strategies that let agents move fast without breaking production code relied on by 7M+ developers.

Prove the approach on real migrations — Micronaut-to-Spring conversions, Lambda-to-container consolidations, API convergence (consolidating overlapping API surfaces onto shared contracts), and strangler-fig domain extractions — before scaling it into a repeatable, multi-agent ""coding squad"" capable of tackling many domains in parallel.

Stay hands-on in the Java/Spring codebase often enough to critically review what the agents produce, recognize when a refactor is architecturally wrong, and correct the agentic loop that generated it — not just the output.

senior-product-manager-carpool-experience-paris-france-14229,Blablacar,Senior Product Manager - Carpool Experience,"Paris, France",False,1790989486,"About BlaBlaCarBlaBlaCar is the world’s leading community-based travel app enabling 27 million members a year to carpool or travel by bus in 21 countries. Our team of 800 employees counts over 50 nationalities and is spread across our 5 global offices, 30% working fully remotely.The role
Carpool Experience covers everything between two members once they have found each other: agreeing on the trip, talking, meeting up, and building trust.
Vision: a carpool experience that feels easy and safe for passengers and drivers, from the first hello to the final goodbye.
Mission: make it simple for members to talk, negotiate, meet up and trust each other.
You own six product areas, used by millions of members every month:

Negotiation. Before booking, passengers can ask the driver for a detour, a lower price or another special request, and add a tip. Drivers accept, decline or make a counter-offer. It launched in France in 2025 and went worldwide in 2026. It is still a new product: what it should become, and how far it can go, is yours to figure out.
Messaging. The chat between drivers and passengers. Next up: Group Chat, and catching up with market standards.
GPS Tracking: both the technical capability as well as features it enables (including sharing ETA on the map, ESC bonus in Spain among others)
Post-Carpool ride XP (claims, ratings etc.). How members build trust in each other. This includes AI Ratings Summary, BlaBlaCar's first consumer-facing GenAI feature.

Communication Service and contact preferences. The platform that sends every push notification, email, SMS and WhatsApp message across the company, plus the settings members use to choose what they receive.
Marketing tools. Braze and deeplinks, used by the CRM and marketing teams.

This is a key scope, and you own its strategy. That comes with high exposure: you present to the Executive Committee every two weeks. You get a direct say in company decisions, and you are expected to bring clear thinking and solid arguments to the table.Your Responsibilities
Set the direction. Build the vision and strategy for your scope, turn it into ambitious OKRs, and get leadership behind them.
Own the numbers. Know your business metrics, reliability targets and costs in detail. Review them every month and act on what they tell you, without being asked.

Shape the future of Negotiation. Work out where its real value is for members and for BlaBlaCar, decide how it should evolve (new use cases such as negotiation after booking, conversion, usage), and prove the impact on passengers (PAX) and GMV.
Ship the next member interactions: Group Chat, live location for both drivers and passengers, and the next version of the Communication Service.
Run experiments and rollouts with discipline. Run A/B tests and country-by-country launches with decision rules set in advance, together with Legal, Privacy and country leads.
Hold your own with the ExCo. Every two weeks, present progress, decisions and trade-offs to the Executive Committee. Take a clear position, defend it, and change it when the evidence calls for it.
Raise the bar of the product team. Share your methods, coach other PMs, and challenge how we work.

You take full ownership of your product's outcomes. You go to the data with a question, spot what changed before anyone flags it, and act on it. You don't wait for direction: you come with a clear proposal, build it with your team and stakeholders, and follow through.

You turn many signals into one clear strategy. You combine data, user research, market moves and tech constraints into one view of where the product should go, not a list of projects. You can explain it in two minutes, it holds from one conversation to the next, and you cut complexity to get more done with less.

You understand the business, not just the product. You know how BlaBlaCar makes money and where your scope fits in. You can give your key metrics, their current level and what moves them without opening a dashboard. You talk about impact on PAX, GMV and costs as naturally as about features.

You have strong opinions and an open mind. You take a clear position without waiting for leadership to take theirs, back it with evidence, and change your view openly when a better argument comes along.

You communicate at a leadership level. You have already owned discussions with C-level or ExCo on strategy and trade-offs, and come out with decisions. You adapt your message to each audience and resolve conflicts constructively.
You have 5+ years of product management, ideally on consumer apps, including at least one scope you owned end to end over several quarters with measurable business impact.&nbsp
You use AI tools in your daily work.&nbsp

column1: forward-deployed-engineer-munich-488819,Tacto,Forward Deployed Engineer,Munich,False,1791006003,"Your ImpactProcurement is over 50% of revenue for industrial companies and their biggest lever for profitability. The hard part is not the software, it is that every customer's reality is different: a different ERP, a different data model, decades of undocumented process. Generic platforms stall exactly there, and that is where most enterprise AI value quietly dies.Forward Deployed Engineering is how we close that gap. You sit inside the customer's environment, build in their production data, and turn what you learn there into product. You are one of the first FDEs at Tacto, so you are not slotting into a playbook, you are writing it while shipping in real accounts.Your TasksBuild in customer environments. Data pipelines, agents, and custom logic on top of the Tacto platform, in real production data.Own the technical side of a deployment. Extraction, mapping, validation, enrichment, until the customer's procurement team can actually work with the result.Be in the room, on site. Run data workshops with key users, debug alongside their IT, and see how a company really buys instead of how the process documentation says it buys.Turn what you learn at the edge into product. Document the pattern and push it to Product and Engineering instead of quietly rebuilding the same one-off for the next customer.Automate your own job. If a step in a deployment can be done by an agent, you build the agent and prove it works.Make it one team. Hold the boundary with Solution Engineering and Customer Value so the customer experiences one Tacto, not three.Your ProfileYou are a builder. You have shipped software, automations, agents, or technical projects that real users relied on.You write code yourself. You are comfortable with Python and SQL and use AI coding tools to move fast.You are AI-native. You have built with LLMs against real data and understand where agents work, where they fail, and where humans still matter.You thrive in messy environments. Incomplete requirements, undocumented data, and conflicting stakeholder input do not stop you from making progress.You can earn customer trust. You explain technical decisions clearly, handle pushback, and do not over-promise.You have 0-4 years of experience with evidence of a steep learning curve through strong technical work, ambitious startups, internships, or things you built from zero.You speak native-level German and fluent English, are based in Munich, and are willing to travel regularly across DACH.Why This Role is AwesomeYou get to combine building software with seeing exactly how it creates value in the real world. You will ship into production, work directly with industrial customers, and turn what you learn at the edge into product improvements. Do this well for 12 to 18 months and you are among the people who defined what Forward Deployed Engineering means at Tacto, with a direct line into the product roadmap and an obvious next step, whether that is leading a team, going deeper into product, or owning a segment.What This Role Is, and Isn'tWe want to be honest about what you are signing up for.This is not an engineering role with customers kept at a safe distance. Customer contact is the job, not a tax on the job. If you want a ticket queue and clean requirements, this is the wrong role.This is not consulting. Nobody here bills days. You are measured on what the customer can do afterwards and on what made it into the platform.It is deliberately broad. If you want to specialise narrowly you will be frustrated here.The deal: prove yourself, deliver real impact, make a strong case for yourself, then we back your next step in every way we can.Why TactoWe bet on young talent and mean it. We consistently back smart, hungry, young people with real ownership early. 70%+ of our Leadership Team was promoted internally: you deliver impact and sky is the limit at Tacto.Backed to win big. We are Sequoia and Index-funded with €50M+ behind us. Our founders sit at the same table as the people defining the global AI agenda. We're building Tacto to be the lighthouse for European industrial AI.A truly AI-native organization, with every resource you could dream of. All the leading AI tools and custom agents at your fingertips, plus dedicated people who keep us at the frontier.High bar, high speed, genuinely fun. You'll be surrounded by extremely smart and ambitious people who set the bar high and push you to get better every week. Intense, fast, and the opposite of boring.A front-row seat in the European startup ecosystem. Weekly exposure to leading founders and operators through internal and external events (Lunch &amp
column2: Learns, hackathons, community gatherings). Check out all upcoming and past events here: https://luma.com/tactoYou'll build something that lasts and that matters. You'll help build the company that keeps European industry competitive for the long term.Our BackgroundTacto is building the intelligence layer that connects AI to the physical world of manufacturing, starting with procurement. AI is transforming every industry, but it stops at the factory gate. The knowledge that holds manufacturing together - part costs, suppliers, materials - is scattered across systems and people. Over 50% of a product's cost originates from suppliers, making procurement the single largest cost lever in manufacturing and the missing connection between the digital and the physical world. Yet it still runs on Excel and legacy systems. We're changing that with our Procurement Intelligence Platform, trusted by hundreds of companies running billions of Euros of material.Based in Munich, we are 100+ passionate builders who are in-office, with high expectations, fast growth, and a lot of fun. We are supported by &gt
column3: €50m from Sequoia, Index, and Europe's leading tech entrepreneurs and industry veterans.Why It MattersManufacturing forms Europe's economic backbone, driving a fourth of Europe's GDP and providing over 30% of jobs. column3: We are pioneering advancements in quantum computing by utilizing trapped ion technology and our proprietary laser-free quantum control methods. Our research and development efforts build on our fully integrated quantum processors that can be fabricated within standard silicon foundries. This unique approach allows us to leverage the highest-performing qubit technology while ensuring scalability and manufacturability using existing semiconductor fabrication technology. We approach quantum computing with a focus on minimizing errors, striving to achieve ultra-low gate errors at scale. Our immediate objective is to develop functional quantum computers within the NISQ regime, aiming to construct fault-tolerant machines that require minimal QEC overhead. Prototyping and characterising coherent control and cooling schemes for trapped-ion qubits using laser and microwave fields.&lt
Calibrating and benchmarking quantum systems, focusing on achieving the highest fidelities for quantum circuit primitives (e.g. ion transport or gate operations) and full circuits.&lt
Validating emerging trap technologies, including integrated electronics and photonics for large-scale architectures.&lt
Analysing experimental data, debug complex hardware/software interactions, and ensure reliability of qubit operations.&lt

Proven expertise in experimental AMO physics or quantum computing. Experience with trapped ions is beneficial though not essential.&lt

Strong collaborative skills, with the ability to work independently and as part of a fast-moving team.&lt

column1: chief-of-staff-to-the-cto-engineering-paris-105211,Pennylane SAS,Chief of Staff to the CTO - Engineering,Paris,False,1790937606,"Are you looking to have an impact on the daily life of millions of entrepreneurs in France (and tomorrow in Europe)?Are you looking for a work environment that values trust, proactivity, and autonomy?Then Pennylane is the right place for you ! Our visionWe aim to become the most beloved financial Operating System of French SMEs and Accounting Firms (and soon, European ones).We help entrepreneurs rid themselves of time-consuming tasks related to accounting and finance while providing them with access to key financial information to assist in making the best decisions for their business. About usPennylane is one of the fastest growing Fintechs in France (and soon to be in Europe!) In 5 years of existence, we’ve managed to :💻 Make ourselves known as a groundbreaking accounting and financial software for small businesses and their accountants💰 Raise a total of €400 millions, including from Sequoia, the famous fund from the Silicon Valley who invested early in companies like Google, Facebook, Airbnb, Stripe, Paypal and much more...👨‍👩‍👧‍👦 Grow from 7 cofounders to 1000 happy Pennylaners : we’re now recognized as one of the greatest places to work in France (and also remotely), with a 4.6/5 rating on Glassdoor.🌍 Build an international environment with more than 25 nationalities, with a strong remote-friendly culture, where 30% of the employees are already working from all parts of Europe🤝 Earn the trust of thousands of customers and accounting firms and obtain outstanding ratings🚀 Already more than 900,000 small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) and over 6000 accounting firms use Pennylane in France! In 2024, we implemented an organizational structure built around business 'tracks'. This approach integrates key stakeholders across marketing, sales, product, and customer care into unified teams focused on specific product lines or client segments. Each track operates as a mini-business, empowered with dedicated resources (e.g., product marketing, data analytics, and operational support) and direct accountability for performance.  Why this role matters at Pennylane As Chief of Staff to the CTO, you operate as a senior leader in the Tech organisation. Your leverage does not come from managing teams but from owning the hardest problems that sit between them, and from being technical enough to earn the trust of the other engineering leaders.You are the person the CTO trusts with ambiguous, org-wide problems. You turn that ambiguity into a clear framing, a decision, an owner and a measurable outcome.This is not a coordination role. You are expected to have opinions on engineering strategy, staffing choices and technical trade-offs, and to defend them in front of the Tech leadership team. Team and Context Pennylane's Tech organisation is 70+ squads, each led by an Engineering Manager working with a PM and a Product Designer. We serve 1.5m+ customers and we want to scale in Europe. At that size, the hard problems are no longer inside a squad: how the organisation plans, how it decides, how it measures itself, how it invests in foundations without stalling product delivery. That is your perimeter.You report directly to Quentin, Co-founder &amp

column1: Chez Doctrine, nous construisons le leader de l’IA juridique en Europe.

Notre conviction ? Le droit ne doit pas être ralenti par des tâches répétitives. Il doit être augmenté par une IA spécialisée, conçue pour comprendre, analyser et produire du raisonnement juridique avec un haut niveau d’exigence.
Notre ambition ? Permettre aux professionnels du droit de gagner en fiabilité, en efficacité et en sérénité, grâce à une plateforme unique, exhaustive et sécurisée.
Aujourd’hui, 27 000 professionnels du droit, répartis dans cinq pays (France, Italie, Allemagne, Espagne, Luxembourg), nous font confiance.
Notre développement est guidé par une approche claire : une vision globale, ancrée dans une compréhension fine des spécificités locales.
Derrière cette ambition, une équipe d’environ 250 personnes, réunies autour d’un même objectif : accompagner les juristes et avocats à toutes les étapes de leur travail, de l’analyse à la rédaction.
Et nous n’en sommes qu’au début.

Contexte du stageDepuis des années, Doctrine propose une fonctionnalité d’envoi de décision de justice en France à ses clients. Cela est une source précieuse de décisions de justice qui permet à Doctrine d’enrichir sa base de données (c'est-à-dire son legal graph) avec des décisions qui n’ont pas pu être ajoutées par nos processus habituels.Le but de ce stage est l’internationalisation de cette fonctionnalité de manière à ce qu’elle soit utilisable dans tous les autres pays où Doctrine est actif (Italie, Allemagne).Les tâches principales seront :
Le développement d’une application minimale pour la revue et validation des décisions de justice mises en ligne par nos utilisateurs pour nos juristes avant leur publication.
La migration du processus legacy d’upload français actuel pour se conformer au processus commun (internationalisé).

Une fois que le processus de mise en ligne de décisions par nos utilisateurs sera internationalisé, le ou la stagiaire pourra travailler sur des tâches d’amélioration de l’application de revue de décisions dans le but d’aider notre équipe de juristes à mieux traiter le volume de décisions mises en ligne.Exemples de pistes d’amélioration (non exhaustif)
Application de techniques d’OCR sur les documents pour faciliter leur validation.
Détection via LLM d’attributs des décisions (niveau de confidentialité, juridiction, domaine du droit, cour, …) pour faciliter leur validation.

Aide au retrait de contenu qui n’est pas le texte de la décision (pages blanches, notification à l’avocat, …).Le ou la stagiaire devra participer à la définition de la solution et sa réalisation. Il ou elle rejoindra l’équipe Italie et sera amené·e à travailler avec les équipes des autres pays (principalement l’équipe France) et l’équipe légale. Il ou elle participera aussi au chapter web (regroupement de tous les développeurs full stack de l’entreprise).

column3: Datadog’s Chaos Engineering team builds systems that surface reliability weaknesses before they become outages. As a Senior Software Engineer, you will initially focus on zonal resilience, building automation that helps services safely evacuate and recover from zonal failures, while also contributing to fault injection, incident replay, gameday orchestration, and reliability tooling. You will work across engineering teams to design systems that safely exercise production failure modes and turn findings into verified remediation. You will also help advance the use of AI and automation to identify, test, and close resilience gaps as Datadog’s software and infrastructure evolve.&lt

At Datadog, we place value in our office culture - the relationships and collaboration it builds and the creativity it brings to the table. We operate as a hybrid workplace to ensure our Datadogs can create a work-life harmony that best fits them.&lt
Build zonal-resilience automation that coordinates safe workload evacuations, switchovers, and recovery in partnership with the teams that own affected services.&lt
Design and build fault-injection systems for production environments, including infrastructure- and application-level testing, incident replay, and controlled resilience experiments.&lt
Develop safeguards such as blast-radius controls, kill switches, validation mechanisms, and rollback paths that keep production experiments contained and reversible.&lt
Build agents and automation that help propose failure scenarios, triage experiment results, and connect reliability findings to tracked remediation and verification.&lt
Lead gamedays from hypothesis and scenario design through execution, documented findings, remediation tracking, and validation of completed fixes.&lt

Design and implement reliable distributed systems, including gRPC services, Kubernetes controllers, and shared platform components, while contributing to technical design and mentoring other engineers.&lt
You have strong distributed systems fundamentals and can reason about consistency, failure modes, backpressure, idempotency, quorum, retries, and failure recovery.&lt
You understand Kubernetes workload lifecycles, including how pods, controllers, scheduling, draining, and eviction interact with resilient system design.&lt
You have experience designing, building, or operating production systems where safety, availability, and controlled failure handling are important.&lt
You communicate complex technical decisions clearly through design documents, runbooks, postmortems, and cross-functional technical discussions.&lt
You are comfortable collaborating across engineering teams to understand unfamiliar systems, identify failure modes, and drive resilience improvements.&lt

Experience with reliability engineering, chaos engineering, zonal failover, AI-assisted operational workflows, traffic interception, or large-scale observability systems is beneficial but not required.&lt

Datadog values people from all walks of life. We know not everyone will meet all the above qualifications on day one. That’s okay. If you’re passionate about technology and want to grow your experience, we encourage you to apply.&lt
Develop deep expertise in distributed systems, production resilience, Kubernetes, and large-scale infrastructure.&lt
Work on reliability systems that operate across Datadog’s production environment and influence how engineering teams design for failure.&lt
Grow your experience designing safe, automated approaches to fault injection, zonal resilience, and incident reproduction.&lt
Explore practical applications of AI and automation to reliability engineering and operational workflows.&lt
Collaborate with engineers across infrastructure, databases, observability, and service teams on complex systems challenges.&lt
Mentor other engineers and contribute to technical designs, engineering practices, and platform strategy.&lt

column1: remote-network-operation-engineer-411432,Share,Network Operation Engineer,Remote,True,1790682013,"Network Operations Engineer1. About the roleShare is the global marketplace for bandwidth. column1: mechanical-engineer-robotics-berlin-303112,Cell Labs,Mechanical Engineer  | Robotics,Berlin,False,1790982025,"We build humanoid systems: full stack, from hardware and electronics to software and manufacturing, all in-house in Berlin.

At Cell Labs, we push the boundary of what robotics can achieve. Our goal is clear: to build systems that empower humans, not replace them. Our technology is already deployed with industry leading customers and partners. Now, our own product is close to launch.
The quiet phase is over. We are looking for people who want to be here early, take ownership, and help us build what others only talk about.
Location: Berlin (on-site) Start: Asap Employment Type: Full-time

column2: CAD: Design and develop mechanical components and assemblies for humanoid systems, from actuators and kinematic mechanisms to sensor mounts and protective enclosures and model them in CAD (e.g. Onshape).

column1: Actuator Kinematics: Design and optimize the kinematic structure of the robot's joints and limbs, including joint layouts, degrees of freedom, ranges of motion, and transmission mechanisms. Select and integrate actuators (motors, gearboxes, encoders) so that torque, speed, and load requirements are met across the full motion range.

Production Readiness: Optimize designs for series production with product requirements, user experience, and target cost in mind. Prepare the handover to manufacturing, including assembly processes, jigs and fixtures, and supplier ramp-up.

column2: Testing: Prototype and validate mechanical systems for performance, safety, and durability. Design and build test rigs for actuators and subassemblies, including endurance and load testing.
Wiring: Integrate PCBs, sensors, and batteries into mechanical assemblies, including cable routing and heat management. Build and solder cables and wiring harnesses for prototypes and test setups.
Materials: Run stress analysis and weight optimization to improve performance and longevity. Research, test, and qualify new materials and processes, such as composites and additive manufacturing.
Specifications: Maintain complete design documentation, including drawings, part specifications, BOMs, and wiring diagrams, with full traceability throughout development.

column1: Background: You studied mechanical engineering, mechatronics, robotics, electrical engineering, or something close to it.
Experience: At least 3 years working on robotic systems, mobile machinery, or similar electromechanical products. What you built matters more to us than where you built it.
Mechanical Design: You've designed complex mechanical systems and understand robot kinematics, actuators, and how mechanical and electrical parts come together in a working robot.

Manufacturing: You know CNC machining, injection molding, sheet metal, and additive manufacturing, and you design with mid- and high-volume production in mind. You've worked with suppliers and brought hardware into production.
Hands-on: You like building things yourself. You solder cables, put together wiring harnesses, build test rigs, and track down problems on the bench.
Tools: You work confidently in Onshape and Autodesk Fusion, including its electronics design tools.
Product lifecycle: Ideally, you've taken at least one hardware product all the way from concept to series production.
How you work: You get a first prototype built quickly and improve from there. You can keep several projects moving at once and know when a design is good enough to move forward.
Languages: Fluent English. German is a plus.

Your work goes into a real robot: The joints, assemblies, and test rigs you design end up in humanoid robots we build ourselves. You take ownership of real subsystems and see them go from CAD to working hardware.

Everything under one roof: Office, workshop, and test rigs are in the same building in Kreuzberg. Your design goes from screen to prototype in days. The electrical and software engineers are a short walk away, not a ticket**.**

Room to grow: Paid learning time and a personal budget for courses, conferences, and the tools you need. You'll get space to try new materials, processes, and ideas, and you'll take on more responsibility as the company grows.
Benefits: A benefits package you put together yourself, covering mobility, health, food, or fitness. Plus one extra paid day off a year for volunteering or a project you care about.

Send us your CV and a few projects you've worked on. Ideally, include a mechanical system you designed and built yourself, with a short note on the challenges and how you solved them. No cover letter needed.
Process: Intro call → Technical deep-dive → On-site visit → Offer

We build robots for everyone, so we want a team that reflects that. We hire on what you can do, and we welcome applications from people who are underrepresented in engineering and tech. If you don't tick every box but think this is your job, apply anyway.

Klub44 ist ein gemeinnütziges Startup im Bereich digitale Jugendbeteiligung. Mit der Klub-App ermöglichen wir es jungen Menschen, ihre eigene Stadt und ihre Vorlieben zu entdecken, und die Welt um sich herum mitzugestalten. Alle jungen Menschen haben das Recht auf ein freies und schöpferisches Leben, daran glauben wir fest.
Nebenbei möchten wir die Schul- und Berufsbildung radikal transformieren.

Mit der Klub-App erhalten Jugendliche ab 12 Jahren einen chancengerechten Zugang zu kostenfreien Freizeit- und Berufsorientierungsangeboten. Außerschulische Standorte – z. B. Jugendclubs, Makerspaces, Orte der kulturellen Bildung – können auf unserer App ihre Angebote direkt und digital an Jugendliche kommunizieren. Das Ganze bauen wir als Game auf: Entdecke deine Stadt, dich selbst, und bekomme dafür Rewards!
Wir ermutigen ausdrücklich Menschen aller Geschlechter, Religionen und sexuellen Orientierungen dazu, sich bei uns zu bewerben!

Als Projektmanager*in Kooperationen bist du die Person, bei der unsere operativen Projekte zusammenlaufen. Kommunen, Schulen und Stiftungen arbeiten mit uns, weil sie ein Ergebnis wollen – du sorgst dafür, dass dieses Ergebnis auch eintritt: im Zeitplan, im Budget, und mit zufriedenen Partnern. Gleichzeitig hast du einen zweiten Auftrag, der genauso wichtig ist: Du führst so viele Projekte wie möglich über unsere Standardprozesse, damit Klub als Plattform skalierbar bleibt und nicht in Sonderlösungen erstickt. Diese Doppelrolle – nach außen verbindlich, nach innen konsequent – ist der Kern des Jobs.
Wir freuen uns auf Mitunternehmer*innen, um gemeinsam mit dem jungen Team und Geschäftsführer Sebastian die Geschicke von Klub44 zu leiten.
Eigenverantwortliche Steuerung unserer laufenden Kooperationsprojekte – von Kick-off bis Abschluss.
Planung von Meilensteinen, Verantwortlichkeiten und Terminen

Erwartungsmanagement mit Verwaltungen, Schulleitungen und Förderpartnern: klar sagen, was geht, und was nicht.
Übersetzungsarbeit zwischen kommunaler Logik und Startup-Tempo – in beide Richtungen.
Onboarding von Kommunen, Schulen und Jugendeinrichtungen entlang unserer Standardprozesse – wiederholbar statt jedes Mal neu.
Weiterentwicklung dieser Prozesse: Playbooks, Templates, Checklisten, Automatisierungen.
Erkennen, wann eine Partneranfrage ein Sonderfall ist – und wann sie in ein neues Standardangebot gehört.
Bewusstes Nein zu Individuallösungen, die uns langfristig teuer werden.
Nachhalten der Projekt-KPIs und transparentes internes Reporting zum Projektstatus.

Ableiten konkreter Maßnahmen aus den Zahlen, nicht nur Dokumentation.
Rückkopplung von Partner-Feedback ins Produkt: Was brauchen Kommunen und Standorte wirklich?
Steuerung externer Partner und Dienstleister im Projektkontext.

Du hast mehrjährige Erfahrung im Projektmanagement und bringst Projekte nachweislich zum Abschluss – idealerweise mit Partnern aus Verwaltung, Bildung, Stiftungen oder NGOs. Arbeitserfahrung in einem Startup ist ein guter Bonus.
Du bist stark in Kooperation und Kommunikation: Du gewinnst Menschen für gemeinsame Ziele und behältst dabei die Interessen von Klub im Blick.

Du arbeitest datenbasiert und bist sicher im Nachhalten von Kennzahlen.

column1: senior-site-reliability-engineer-ceph-on-prem-cloud-storage-koln-412596,gridscale GmbH,Senior Site Reliability Engineer - Ceph / On-Prem Cloud Storage (m/f/d),Köln,False,1790940011,"Your RoleYou will help us build, operate and industrialize the storage foundation of our on-premise cloud platform. As part of a small, experienced team, you will own the Ceph clusters behind our block, object and file storage services – essentially the storage every customer workload eventually lands on. The platform is still actively being built, which means you will have real influence on the storage architecture, hardware lifecycle, automation strategy and technical direction. The role goes beyond Ceph itself: you will regularly work across bare metal, networking, OpenStack, Kubernetes and GitOps. As a Senior Engineer, you take ownership of your area and help make storage predictable, durable and highly automated as we scale into the petabytesUnser Tech Stack 🚀· Ceph · OpenStack · Kubernetes · KVM · Linux · Bare Metal · Ansible · Terraform · Go · Cinder ·Neutron · Nova · RBD · Cilium · RGW/ S3 · Prometheus/ Grafana · FluxCD / ArgoCD · Git· Python · Claude Code · Cursor · Agentic Coding ToolingYour ResponsibilitiesDesign, operate and evolve our Ceph clusters for block, object / S3 and file storage - from CRUSH topology and failure domains to pool design, placement groups, erasure coding, capacity headroom and performance.Own the storage hardware lifecycle end to end – from qualification and burn-in through firmware, controller and disk health to OSD add/drain/replace, node retirement and hardware refresh. A key part of the job is automating these processes without creating tenant-visible impact.Automate the provisioning of storage nodes on OpenStack-managed bare metal, working with Ironic, RAID and disk configuration, SEDs, provider networks and VLANs. You will also own the artefact path around images, package mirrors, certificates and other dependencies needed to bring up clusters in environments with tightly controlled external connectivity.Run upgrades, rebalancing and reconfigurations as routine production operations, evolve our Infrastructure as Code and GitOps setup with Ansible, Terraform and FluxCD / ArgoCD, and make sure storage integrates cleanly with both OpenStack and Kubernetes.Own capacity planning and growth forecasting, use telemetry to understand real consumption, and build out monitoring, testing and failure-injection around performance, durability and security.AI-assisted engineering is simply part of how we work today. You use LLMs and agentic tools where they genuinely help – across development, testing, reviews, incident triage, knowledge retrieval or automation - and help us push further into self-healing and auto-remediation.Act as a technical reference and sparring partner across Ceph, storage, automation and AI tooling, document technical decisions and share your knowledge with the team.What we offerExceptional team spirit across all departments and national borders

They treat these capabilities as internal products: defining the interfaces other teams build against and remaining accountable for their reliability, evolution, and operation over time.The work is to turn complex capabilities such as model access, agent execution, authorization, queues, integrations, document processing, and sandboxed compute into stable, reusable building blocks. Each capability needs a clear contract and must be able to evolve without forcing coordinated changes across the rest of the product.You own a service from design through long-term operation. When a service requires a new underlying mechanism, you work with Systems Engineers while remaining accountable for the service boundary and lifecycle.What you might work onCurrent platform work includes:A durable agent runtime. This also includes deterministic context reconstruction, compaction, and prompt-cache efficiency.The Model Gateway. We are building one inference boundary for every Langdock product, with a model-agnostic API over managed and customer-provided models. The work includes provider adapters, routing across accounts and regions, rate limits, bounded fallback, streaming safety, usage tracking, and a control plane.Shared services with explicit contracts. We are moving selected capabilities out of a TypeScript monolith into independently operated services with Protobuf and gRPC contracts inside one Bazel monorepo. Our authorization service, written in Go with embedded SpiceDB, is one example: the migration uses an outbox, shadow comparisons on production traffic, and consistency tokens before it becomes authoritative.The integration and tool platform. Langdock already connects to external services through REST APIs, Model Context Protocol (MCP), and agent-to-agent (A2A) communication. The platform work is to make authentication, token refresh, rate limits, approvals, outbound network safety, and tool execution consistent across these paths.Code execution as a shared service. Langdock already runs untrusted JavaScript, Bash, and Python through separate execution environments. Platform work includes defining a consistent execution API, lifecycle, permission model, resource budgets, and operational boundary, while partnering with Systems Engineers on the underlying isolation and scheduling mechanisms.Production confidence for shared systems. Platform changes need evidence before rollout. Current work includes a reusable load-testing system for HTTP, gRPC, and streaming workloads

Well, it isn’t, it is actually quite real!Read on!

If you’ve already heard about us, you’re probably reading this because you’re tired of the typical, chaotic ways of doing things in construction. But in case you haven’t, we’re a high-end project management consultancy and tech developer with a focus on upgrading the way construction projects are delivered.
Improving construction strengthens the very foundation of human civilisation. (Check out our short film about it.)

We bring transparency and control to projects through a pragmatic mix of the latest tech, our own processes, and a big dose of common sense. We then take our deep understanding of these projects and we invest heavily into developing the digital solutions that anyone can use to deliver their projects better. (Check out Shape, our construction management tech, to see what we’re doing.)

The core of all this is our true secret sauce: our people. We only recruit the very best, both in capability and personality. We’re deeply focused on designing a new type of organisation that’s optimised for the flourishing of the people in the team first and foremost. People who join us develop fast as a whole person in ways they never imagined. (Read more about our vision and missions.)

This approach has allowed us to grow from just two people in 2017 to over 220 today. We have a stable, repeat client base across infrastructure and complex building projects in the UK and internationally, and we’re still growing fast. Joining us isn’t just some “job”. It’s a transformative educational experience. We challenge you to be your best self in all aspects of life. There are many diverse and interesting challenges available. It’s up to you to guide yourself into whichever areas you’re most interested – we’ll enable it.&nbsp
(Get to know us better by watching a few more of our videos.)
Core values for a good life
A life of human flourishing is all about meaningful relationships and challenging yourself to create a positive impact, so our values reflect the four levels of relationships that each of us has:
- Grow yourself – your relationship with yourself&nbsp
- Care about people – your relationship with others around you&nbsp
- Execute to greatness – your relationship with your team&nbsp
- Build civilisation – your relationship with humanity and the world&nbsp
We enshrined our values in our vision:
We exist so that everyone in our team can flourish in a high-impact community that:
- Inspires us to develop ourselves to become better humans&nbsp
- Empowers us to pursue our own learning adventures&nbsp
By first doing this, we can achieve the highest levels of value for the world.
And enable the achievement of our vision through our two missions:
- To fully digitalise the construction of human civilisation&nbsp
- To create a new type of organisation that enables human flourishing while delivering a huge positive impact on society

You will be enhancing the delivery of the most complex and interesting projects in the world through the power of project planning. You will be a senior leader in our team pushing the discipline to new heights not only within Laminar but within the industry in general.

This role is part of our Project Management Consultancy which focuses on:- Understanding what the real problems of projects are- Implementing the best solutions to those problems- Developing scalable best practices, tools and technology

More specifically you will be part of our Project Planning Discipline Team who are industry leaders in the planning of complex construction projects. Your initial leader will be one of our planning discipline directors.

column1: remote-regional-sales-manager-dach-8213,Everfield,"Regional Sales Manager, DACH (m/w/d)",Germany - Remote,False,1790898011,"Regional Sales Manager, DACH (m/w/d)Regional Role · Remote, based in the DACH region · Reports to: Sales DirectorAbout EverfieldEverfield acquires and builds vertical SaaS businesses across Europe. Our portfolio spans more than 40 companies serving niche markets where software is mission-critical. We take a long-term ownership approach: we buy, invest, and build. We don't flip. Seven companies are in DACH, and we expect continuous growth in portfolio size and performance across all regions.We are building a small, high-impact HQ revenue team responsible for lifting the commercial capability of our portfolio companies: setting standards, identifying risk, and accelerating performance. The role reports to Everfield's Sales Director, who owns consistency of the revenue system across all regions, and works day to day with the region's General Director and the CEOs of its Business Units.The OpportunityThe Regional Sales Manager (RSM) is a cluster-level revenue operator responsible for improving sales execution and accelerating organic revenue growth across a group of portfolio companies. The role partners directly with CEOs and Business Unit leaders to strengthen pipeline discipline, improve forecast accuracy, and raise commercial maturity across the region.This is not purely an advisory role. Alongside the regional remit, the RSM is expected to take direct sales management responsibility inside Business Units where that is the fastest route to growth, giving smaller commercial teams access to experienced sales leadership they would not otherwise have. As the region scales, the ambition is that one person can hold the sales management role on behalf of several Business Units at once, applying a standard across all of them.Success is reflected in improved revenue predictability, stronger pipeline discipline, and sustained bookings growth across Business Units.How the Role Operates• Two levels, one standard. The regional remit is constant: diagnostics, pipeline discipline, forecast integrity, and commercial governance across every Business Unit in the cluster. Beyond it, the role flexes. In some Business Units you will coach and support an existing sales manager. In others you will hold the sales management role yourself.• Direct team leadership where it is needed. Where you act as sales manager, you own the team, the pipeline, the forecast, and the number, in the same way a local sales manager would, and you report into that Business Unit's CEO for delivery while remaining accountable to Everfield for how the work is done.• You are not a seller. You do not carry a personal quota and you are not measured on deals you close yourself. You are measured on what the teams you lead and support deliver.• Reporting. You report to Everfield's Sales Director for standards, priorities, and development. The role is a shared resource for the region rather than a function serving any single Business Unit, acting in close partnership with Group Directors, CEOs, and sales teams.What You Will DoSales Execution &amp
column2: Commercial Acceleration• Drive new and expansion bookings growth across the cluster, with consistent attention to prospecting, opportunity development, and account growth.• Act as sales manager for one or more Business Units: run the weekly rhythm, set priorities, coach the team, and hold sellers to their number.• Reduce volatility in bookings performance and increase revenue consistency across the cluster.• Strengthen proactive sales behaviour across outbound, account expansion, renewals and opportunity reactivation.• Improve sales execution across the full funnel, from lead generation through to closing and account retention.• Embed sales methodology and qualification standards, and hold teams to them through evidence rather than instruction.• Lead deal/pipeline reviews and targeted coaching to improve win rates, shorten cycle times, and build seller capability.Pipeline Discipline &amp
column3: Forecast Integrity• Improve forecast reliability across Business Units, working toward 5% variance or better.• Define and apply opportunity qualification standards and run structured pipeline reviews.• Ensure pipeline visibility reflects realistic execution capacity, and raise revenue risks early to Business Units and Everfield leadership, always paired with a recommended course of action rather than an open flag.• Monitor sustained underperformance patterns and ensure corrective action plans are implemented in time to matter.Revenue Standards &amp

column2: we are now entering our next phase of growth. From our headquarters on Zürich's Bahnhofstrasse, we're expanding globally, with a growing presence across Europe and North America. Join us and help make autonomous operations the new standard. LocationThis is a full-time position based in Munich or Cologne. Following a comprehensive onboarding period at our HQ in central Zurich (minimum one month), you will work from your home location, with regular visits to customers across the DACH region.Team collaboration matters a lot to us. You will regularly spend time with the team in person, in Zurich and at our hubs, for team days, all-hands and offsites. These visits are financially supported by blp.Your MissionOn our largest global rollouts, connectivity is what makes or breaks the program.These customers run several ERP systems across many entities and countries, with interfaces, master data and process variants that have grown over decades. Whether blp is usable on day one, and whether the first go-live holds its date, depends more on getting that landscape right than on almost anything else. You are the person who makes sure it is right. You sit opposite the customer's enterprise architects and IT leads, understand what their landscape actually does rather than what the documentation says, and shape the technical solution with them.Getting this right is relentless project management as much as architecture. Requirements on a landscape this size never arrive clear. You chase them until they are: pushing the customer's IT organization for answers, going back when an answer is vague, and refusing to let an assumption stand in for a decision. You spot the major developments and the roadblocks early, while there is still time to do something about them, and you put them in front of the Senior Project Manager and into the steering committee rather than discovering them in test.When you raise something, you bring the way through it. You prepare the discussion with the customer, make the implications clear in their language, and come with options. ""We cannot do that and we will miss the go-live"" is not the job. Working out what would make it possible, and what it costs, is. Where something exceeds the standard you prepare the decision rather than take it alone: options, effort, consequences, and a clear recommendation for the steering committee or for our engineering leadership.You are the strong technical counterpart for the customer's IT organization and for the Senior Project Manager. Both rely on you to know what is actually true. You work primarily up to the first go-live, where the solution design is either right or expensive, and you are staffed by process and landscape complexity rather than by deal size.A word on what you build. Our integration layer works like an iPaaS: connections are assembled as configuration on our own platform, specific to that customer, rather than written as code. You work in that layer yourself, so this is a hands-on role, and you document what you have configured so that the next person can understand and maintain it. What you do not do is write code that ships with the product. That distinction is what keeps a customer-specific solution from quietly becoming everyone's problem.Two roles sit either side of you and the handoffs are clean.With the Integrations Engineer: you define what the connection has to do and why, they build and operate it at that customer and own whether it runs. You hand them a specification, they come back with questions and constraints from the real system, and you resolve them together. When something breaks in their environment, it is theirs. When something is wrong in what was asked for, it is yours.With the Product Engineer: when a requirement cannot be met in configuration, or when the same requirement has now appeared at the third customer, you make the case for building it into the product. You write the specification, they build it, and you are the one who confirms it actually solves the customer problem it came from. After that it is part of the standard and you configure against it like anything else.Key ResponsibilitiesShape the technical solution with the customer, including their enterprise architects and IT leads.Turn business requirements into a clear, implementable specification.Drive requirements to clarity, relentlessly. Chase the customer's IT organization until an answer is specific enough to build on.Configure integrations on our platform where the standard covers it, and document what you have configured.Identify precisely where the standard does not cover a requirement, and judge whether it belongs in configuration or in the product.Identify major development needs and technical roadblocks early, and escalate them to the Senior Project Manager and into the steering committee while there is still time.Prepare those discussions with the customer: make the implications clear, and bring options rather than a refusal.Prepare scope decisions with options, effort and consequences, and bring a clear recommendation to the steering committee or to our engineering leadership.Specify what the Integrations Engineer builds at the customer, and resolve the constraints they bring back from the real system.Make the case for what should be built once for everyone, hand it to our Product Engineers with a proper specification, and confirm it solves the problem it came from.Support the Senior Project Manager and Project Manager on technical feasibility, effort and sequencing.Stay on the account through the first go-live, and hand over a solution design that is documented and maintainable.Feed recurring customer requirements back to Product so the standard grows in the right direction.What We're Really Looking ForThe following key attributes ensure success in this role:Relentless on Clarity – You do not accept a vague answer as an answer, and you keep going until the requirement is specific enough to build on.Architectural Judgment – You can tell the difference between a requirement that deserves a custom solution and one that deserves a conversation.Credibility with Architects – You hold your own with a customer's enterprise architect and earn their trust rather than deferring to them.Clear Recommendations – You frame a difficult scope question so that the people who decide can actually decide, and you say plainly what you would do.Translation – You move between a business requirement and a technical design in both directions without losing anything.Long-Term Thinking – You design for what the customer will need in two years, not only for what unblocks the current wave.What You BringMaster's degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering, or a related field.4+ years of experience in solution design, technical consulting, enterprise integration or a technical product role.Solid understanding of enterprise system landscapes: ERP systems, interfaces, master data, and how data actually moves between them.Hands-on experience configuring integrations on an integration platform, or comparable low-code or configuration-driven work.Experience writing specifications that engineers can build from without a translation layer.Track record of driving technical clarity in a project setting, including escalating early and constructively.Comfortable in customer-facing technical discussions with senior IT stakeholders.Fluent in German and English, spoken and written.Bonus points for hands-on experience with SAP, Microsoft Dynamics or comparable ERP systems, or with e-invoicing and EDI standards.BenefitsHigh ownership environment – you shape your projects, outcomes, and career path.Impact at scale – your work powers automation across global enterprises.Cross-functional exposure – work with engineers, data scientists, and business leaders daily.Real growth – fast-paced environment, steep learning curve, and structured career progression.Employee ownership – be part of a majority employee-owned company with a best-in-class stock option program.Amazing team – become part of a driven and collaborative group of innovators.Technology exposure – be at the forefront of AI and enjoy continuous learning opportunities.Visits &amp

column1: langfuse-product-engineer-integrations-germany-129825,Clickhouse,"Langfuse - Product Engineer, Integrations",Germany,False,1790887209,"Why Integrations Engineering at LangfuseYour work puts Langfuse into developers’ hands.Our SDKs are downloaded 26M+ times per month, and for many developers the first thing they touch is an integration — a few lines of code that connect their favorite framework to Langfuse. column1: junior-creative-director-design-brand-munchen-493447,Vogel,(Junior) Creative Director – Design & Brand (m/w/d),München,False,1790887207,"Deine RolleDie Beratungsbranche in Deutschland sieht überall gleich aus. Gleiche Bildwelten, gleiche Stockfotos, gleiche Blautöne, gleiche Sprache. Marke ist in diesem Markt praktisch unbesetzt.Vogel ist eine der erfolgreichsten mittelständischen Beratungsgesellschaften in Deutschland — mehrere Tausend mittelständische Unternehmen vertrauen uns ihre Steuer-, kaufmännischen und strategischen Themen an. Diesen Markt gewinnt nicht, wer den besseren Fachaufsatz schreibt, sondern wer als Marke dauerhaft präsent ist und den Markt anführt — bei Unternehmern genauso wie bei den Menschen, die wir für uns gewinnen wollen. Du kommst aus einer Agentur, einem eigenen Studio oder von einer Marke mit starkem visuellem System. Du wechselst, weil du dort immer nur einen Teilbereich verantwortest — eine Kampagne, ein Relaunch, eine Strecke im System — und nie die Marke als Ganzes samt der Experience dahinter verantworten und führen darfst. Genau das willst du: die volle visuelle Verantwortung, mit einem Auftraggeber, der dir das Urteil nicht wegnimmt.Die Rolle ist bewusst nach unten offen. Wenn du gerade aus einem starken Gestaltungsstudium oder einer gestalterischen Ausbildung kommst und deine Mappe das visuelle Urteil und die Systemtiefe zeigt, die diese Rolle braucht, bist du hier richtig — du startest dann am unteren Ende der Spanne, arbeitest zunächst an Teilen des Systems und wächst in die volle Verantwortung hinein. Das Portfolio entscheidet, nicht das Jahr des Abschlusses. Bei Vogel findest du beides: Strukturen, die tragen, und ein Setup, das jeden Tag nach vorne geht. Kein Konzern-Korsett. Kein Aufbau-Versprechen ohne Boden.Du verantwortest das gesamte visuelle System von Vogel und der weiteren Marken, die daneben entstehen — Print, Digital, Raum, Bewegtbild, Experience. column1: senior-marketing-manager-frankfurt-223999,Emma – The Sleep Company,(Senior) Marketing Manager,Frankfurt,False,1790875493,"Ready to lead, disrupt and reinvent the sleep industry?

We are Emma – The Sleep Company. Founded in 2015, we have grown into the world’s largest direct-to-consumer (D2C) sleep brand, with a presence in over 20 markets and more than 35 Emma stores across Europe.

Our mission is simple: to develop sleep comfort products that empower our customers to awaken their best every day. Today, our products are trusted by millions and recommended by leading consumer associations worldwide.

It’s our people who bring this mission to life. At Emma, you’ll join a driven, international team that values ownership, collaboration, and continuous knowledge sharing. With colleagues from over 70 nationalities, we combine diverse perspectives with a shared ambition to learn, grow, and create lasting impact, together.
Ready to awaken your best with us?&nbsp

We are looking for a Performance Marketing Manager to drive online revenue growth for Emma's EU Ecommerce team. You will be responsible for owning paid channels campaigns end to end, so that every euro invested delivers a measurable return.
You'll work closely with key stakeholders, ranging from Global Performance Marketing and Creative Marketing to Brand Marketing and the different EU Ecommerce country teams.
Own paid campaigns across Paid Search, Paid Social, Affiliates, Influencer, CRM and TV (linear and CTV), from strategy through execution to continuous optimization.
Run A/B tests across creatives, audiences and landing pages, and turn the results into repeatable playbooks that raise performance across your channels and your market.
Stay ahead of platform changes, algorithm updates and market trends, and proactively bring new tools, tactics and opportunities to the team.
Define and drive performance targets such as ROAS, CPA and conversion rate, and turn data from attribution tools and in-house dashboards into clear strategic decisions.
Own your revenue target and deliver local, regional or global projects on time, becoming the go-to expert for the channels you own.
Collaborate with global performance and creative teams on ad messaging, budget allocation and channel mix to maximize return on every euro invested.
Partner with Sales to drive commercial performance across products and categories in your market, aligning campaign plans with commercial priorities.
You have a Bachelor's or Master's degree in Marketing, Finance, Business Administration or Engineering, which gives you a solid base for data-driven decisions.
You have 3+ years of relevant in-house experience in B2C Ecommerce, ideally in FMCG, consumer goods or online services, with ownership of paid performance channels.
You bring strong analytical skills and a strategic understanding of paid channels, turning performance data into decisions that grow revenue and improve ROAS.
You have project management experience, having delivered local, regional or global projects on time while aligning multiple stakeholders along the way.
You are proactive and self-reflective: you bring ideas instead of waiting for tasks, take feedback well and own your channels with autonomy.
You collaborate well and communicate in a structured way, building a strong network across teams, agencies and partners to deliver shared results.
You are fluent in English and German.
The opportunity to create real impact, take ownership and accountability, and drive meaningful change.
Continuous learning and development through hands-on experience, mentoring, formal training, and access to tools such as our Learning Hub and Nilo.
A collaborative community of smart, driven people where you learn, contribute, and connect, every day and through team events.
A global environment, working daily with diverse perspectives across 4 offices and 70+ nationalities.
25 vacation days per year, with 1 extra day per year worked (until a limit of 30 days per year).
A flexible hybrid setup with up to 22 remote days per quarter, and offices in Gutleutviertel - Frankfurt.

We are on a mission to become No.1 in the world of sleep, and we’re looking for driven, ambitious people to help us shape what’s next. If you’re curious, hands-on, and ready to challenge the status quo, you’ll find the space here to make things happen and create real impact. &nbsp

We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer and are committed to building an inclusive workplace. We celebrate diversity and consider all qualified applicants regardless of race, ethnic origin, religion or belief, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, disability, or age.&nbsp
Our aim is to get back to you within a few days. Due to the high volume of applications, there may be slight delays, but we’ll get back to you as soon as possible.

Du übernimmst die Verantwortung für alle People Operations Themen in Deinem festen Betreuungsbereich und bist eine verlässliche Ansprechperson für Mitarbeitende und Führungskräfte.

Du steuerst unsere zentralen administrativen Prozesse entlang der Employee Journey – von Verträgen und Bescheinigungen über das Abwesenheitsmanagement bis hin zu Visa-Prozessen gemeinsam mit unserer externen Agentur.

Du hinterfragst bestehende Prozesse, erkennst Möglichkeiten zur Vereinfachung und setzt deine Ideen in pragmatische und nachhaltige Lösungen um.
Du behältst Änderungen im Arbeitsrecht und Best Practices im People-Operations-Bereich im Blick und leitest daraus klare Maßnahmen für bonial ab.
Als Teil des Teams unterstützt Du regelmäßig unsere Bürotage und Vor-Ort-Termine, zum Beispiel Onboardings und Unterschriftentermine.
Du bringst umfangreiche Berufserfahrung in People Operations, HR-Administration oder einer vergleichbaren generalistischen HR-Rolle mit.
Du verstehst, was gute Datenqualität, verlässliche Prozesse und ein reibungsloses Tagesgeschäft brauchen – und wie diese Themen zusammenspielen.

column1: Spannendes Umfeld für Deine berufliche Entwicklung – Wir unterstützen Dich stark in Deiner beruflichen Entwicklung, gestützt von einer Feedback-Kultur, die Dir hilft, Deine Stärken und Chancen zu erkennen.

A company with 100,000 employees can have thousands of operational challenges across its business units. Somewhere outside that organisation, a startup has probably already built part of the solution. Getting those two things to meet still happens through spreadsheets, long email threads, and meetings whose primary output is another meeting.GlassDollar OS is the operating system for venture clienting: problem → startup discovery → evaluation → PoC → adoption, in one repeatable workflow.Our customers are some of Europe's largest organisations, so the software has to move quickly and behave like something an enterprise can depend on. That tension creates the interesting engineering problems.What we're looking forYou can take a problem further than the ticket. Work often starts with something incomplete, like ""customers need a better way to manage X"". You'll shape the problem with product, challenge assumptions, and decide what belongs in this iteration. Strong opinions about what we build, not only how, are expected here.You care about product. You want to know who you're building for, why the problem matters, and what success looks like. That context should shape your technical decisions.You have technical judgement. There is rarely one correct architecture. You know when the boring solution beats the ambitious one, when an abstraction helps and when it hides the problem, and when a small feature is about to create six months of technical debt. We expect you to reason about API boundaries, data models, permissions, performance, failure modes, testing, observability, and rollout, and to raise concerns with a clear argument attached.You make the system better, not just the feature. You fix the spreading pattern rather than the single instance, make an API easier for the next person, and improve tests because the current setup makes everyone afraid to deploy. Your impact should show beyond the pull requests with your name on them.You can work across the stack. What happens with old data, or when the API fails halfway through? We use Playwright and Jest alongside reviews and monitoring. The goal isn't coverage, it's confidence.You communicate like your decisions will matter later. column1: senior-conversion-design-analyst-berlin-228619,Good Hood Gmbh,Senior Conversion Design Analyst (f/m/d),Berlin,False,1790809778,"Your missionWe're looking for a Senior Conversion Design Analyst who decides with evidence. You will frame real user problems based on qualitative and quantitative data, design a part of our product, form a view about what should change, build the experiment that tests it, and analyze the results yourself. You will sit inside the product delivery team that focuses on user growth, working closely with the person accountable for that part of the business and with the engineers building it. And you will not be doing it alone: You join a group of Conversion Design Analysts across the company who work the same way and hold each other's standards.English is our working language. German matters here too: You will be designing flows that German-speaking users read.Concretely, you will:Design experiences grounded in real user needs and real neighbourhood life. Your job is to design flows and screens that are highly usable and intuitive and that earn their place by adding measurable value, not just because we can build them.Frame the real problem before solving it. A well-framed problem is half the battleRun the experiment, and read it honestly. Design a testable change, get it instrumented properly, and analyse the outcome. That includes reporting the tests that did not work, and saying what you would do differently.Talk to neighbours. Experiments tell you what happened, not what people needed. You will spend real time with the people who use this, because you cannot A/B test your way to understanding somebody.Direct AI, and spend your judgment where it counts. AI produces a lot of our first-pass design. You will brief it, push back on it, and hold the quality bar, so your own hours go to the thinking a model cannot do. Argue for cutting things. Adding is easy. You will help decide what earns its place and what should be removed, and be willing to make the case for less.Your profileYou practice product design and analytics. You might come from an analyst background and bring a love of design and design thinking, or vice versa.You have technical know-how and experience in setting up and evaluating experiments in an A/B testing tool, constructing the needed dashboards for the problem space you are working on and use our design system tooling.With sufficient data literacy, you get your own numbers through SQL query. You don’t need to be able to run R, but you understand what Bayesian vs. frequentist is about and why you do a power analysis before launching an experiment. You care about craft and are attentive to details. You can tell the difference between good enough and actually good and you design experiences people do not have to think about.You are fluent with AI tools. column1: senior-software-engineer-platform-infrastructure-berlin-56536,Holoplot,Senior Software Engineer - Platform & Infrastructure (f/m/d),Berlin,False,1790788149,"The product you will work onThe HOLOPLOT Matrix Array is a new type of sound system built around precise, software-defined control of sound in three dimensions - grounded in physics and implemented through a combination of custom hardware and purpose-built software. HOLOPLOT deployed Matrix Arrays in various venues, including the Sphere in Las Vegas - the world’s most advanced entertainment venue and, notably, home to the world’s largest audio installation in entertainment. Audio processing in HOLOPLOT systems is distributed: every loudspeaker runs embedded Linux, and hundreds of them have to be configured, coordinated, monitored, and updated as one system. This is enabled by multiple open source and in-house developed services running on an on-premises Kubernetes cluster. AWS-hosted services connect venues to remote monitoring, telemetry, and configuration. Many venues are air-gapped or only intermittently connected for remote servicing, and that constraint shapes most of the design decisions in the platform.The ideal candidate isWe are looking for a Senior Software Engineer who builds the platform our sound systems run on, and who takes responsibility for how it behaves in production.This is a software engineering role first. You will spend your time writing software, either with your own team or embedded with one of the other HOLOPLOT teams: services, controllers, agents, and tooling that provision, configure, observe, and update our systems. Our infrastructure is defined as code and evolves through the same review and release process as the rest of our software. You design the operational side, you build it, and you are on call when it misbehaves in the field.Your role and responsibilitiesYou will join the team that owns the platform underneath our installations and connected services, working alongside backend, embedded, and frontend engineers who are organized in cross-functional product teams.Build the platformArchitect and implement services to provision, configure, and manage server fleets across AWS and local clusters.Create control-plane logic for venue systems to ensure consistency, health monitoring, rollout management, and recovery, even during uplink disruptions.Establish end-to-end provisioning workflows for embedded Linux hardware, spanning from initial manufacturing to customer deployment.Enhance update processes to streamline software deployments for active customer installations.Develop APIs and developer tooling that empower engineering teams to independently deploy, observe, and troubleshoot their services.Embed telemetry capabilities into the platform to facilitate remote diagnosis of venue system behavior.Run what you buildOwn the AWS infrastructure behind our connected services: remote access, access control, telemetry ingestion, remote backup, secret management, and monitoring. All of it is infrastructure as code.Operate and evolve the on-premises Kubernetes footprint at venues, including air-gapped and intermittently connected installations.Monitor large environments, investigate problems across the software/hardware boundary, and turn each incident into a fix in the code.Be part of a compensated on-call rotationSet the technical directionAdvise and collaborate with product teams on building distributed systems that are scalable, secure, and observable, and review their designs with production reality in mind.Research and introduce tools and technologies where they measurably improve how we build and operate.Contribute back to the open-source projects we depend on, through issues and fixes.What you need to succeed in this roleSeveral years of professional software engineering experience, most of it spent designing and shipping production systems.Fluency in software engineering as a craft: concurrency, error handling, testing, and designing APIs that other teams build on.Working knowledge of the Kubernetes control plane and the operator/controller pattern, including how clusters behave when they are unhealthy.Hands-on experience with AWS, and a firm belief in infrastructure as code. Terraform and Ansible are what we use today.Comfort across several languages, and the ability to pick up a new one when the problem calls for it. Our platform work is mostly Go and Python, with Rust and C++ elsewhere in the stack.Experience building distributed systems, and a clear understanding of how they fail: partitions, partial rollouts, clock skew, retries, and reconciliation.A good sense for software architecture and maintainability, and the habit of writing code that colleagues can pick up and change.A strong command of Linux, scripting, and automation.Experience instrumenting software for telemetry and using it to answer real questions about running systems.Good judgment about what to automate and what to leave alone.Strong communication skills in English. You can explain a design or a failure clearly to engineers, product stakeholders, and non-specialists.Willingness to take part in compensated on-call and weekend work when installations need it.A can-do mentality, an eye for detail, and the courage to take on problems outside your comfort zone.Experience in using AI for engineering.Nice to havesExperience with NATS, Prometheus/Thanos, or PostgreSQL in production.Experience with air-gapped or intermittently connected installations.Experience running Kubernetes in production, not only deploying to it.Experience with embedded Linux, device fleet management, or IoT security.Networking depth: multicast at scale, WireGuard, BGP, IPv6.Experience in the audio, broadcast, or live events industry.Contributions to open-source infrastructure projectsWe offer youAt HOLOPLOT we work in a flexible hybrid setup with trust-based working hours, giving you the freedom to organise your day in a way that supports focus, deep work and balance. Pay is competitive and fair, and we offer perks and benefits such as subsidised public transport, lunch allowances, Urban Sports and a company pension scheme.You’ll join an international, open-minded team across software, hardware, product and research, in an environment with plenty of autonomy and ownership.
